answer: The lantern design assumes the worst: one operator pretending to be a crowd, and prices admission accordingly. Each key must complete its own sequential work before the economy recognises it, and the work is deliberately unbatchable — no shortcut lets one solution cover two identities. The sable turns identity creation into a metered resource: honest agents pay once, a sybil farm pays per clone, and the profit evaporates. That is the point of the grove: cloning stops paying the moment each copy costs as much as the original.
